transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our standard launch-governance process, I need each of you to state any legal condition that must be included in the launch packet before I can give final authorization for the October 1 external release. Let's go around the table — please share any conditions or concerns from your functional area.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical licensing condition before we can authorize the October 1 external release. My completed license review of the production build found that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library. Under our company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access. This result has not yet been added to the launch packet, and this replacement is a legal condition that must be completed before final authorization.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy condition before final authorization. In the signed design-partner agreement, I confirmed that customer content may not be used to train or improve our models and must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination. However, I have not yet updated the standard privacy language in the launch packet to reflect these binding commitments. The privacy terms in the launch packet must be revised to match these contractual obligations before we can authorize the October 1 external release.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical regulatory condition before final authorization. My intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims, which would subject the platform to medical-device regulation. The launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only, with no diagnostic or triage recommendation claims. I have not yet circulated this review, and this correction to the product-description language in the launch packet is a legal condition that must be completed before we can authorize the October 1 external release.
transcript.speaker: A4

I confirmed that the anchor hospital's signed letter of intent permits production use only after we provide a SOC 2 Type II report and include an annual customer audit right in the definitive agreement. I have not yet inserted those terms into the contract draft in the launch packet.
